title: Automate publish & maintenance of verified perf profiles with slice-aware pinning
creator: Aisha Carter
description:
Problem statement: Onboarding new models and publishing Redwood-verified performance profiles is currently a semi-manual process. We lack consistent slice-aware pin policies, regional cost normalization, and an automated re-verification cadence. Consequences: stale or overly optimistic profiles leading to incorrect routing, cost surprises for customers, and rollback churn during rollouts.

Goal: Deliver an automated pipeline and operational playbook that publishes verified performance profiles (latency, throughput, cost) to the performance catalog, attaches slice metadata (sequence length, batch-size, region, padding distribution), and enforces pinning rules that are slice-aware. The pipeline should also schedule periodic re-verification jobs and surface drift alerts into the Console and Slack.

Scope:
- Define canonical slice taxonomy and mandatory signals to record with each profile (latency p50/p95, throughput QPS, tokens/sec, cost-per-token normalized by region, sample size, hw config, quantization).
- Implement CI-driven profile publish flow that consumes synthetic and sampled production runs, produces an auditable signature, and pushes a signed manifest to the profile registry.
- Add automated pin policy that maps customer pin intents to slices (e.g., "low-latency-small-batch-eu-west-1" -> pin to variant X).
- Create a lightweight rollback & fallback policy tied to profile health (regression thresholds and canary hooks).
- Integrate alerts into the Console: per-profile health timeline, recent verifications, drift score, and recommended actions.
- Add cost-normalization step to compare across regions and hardware (GBP/USD/EUR) and embed normalized-cost in profile metadata.
- Provide docs and runbook for SRE/Support with common troubleshooting queries and link to synthetic load harness (GitHub: redwood/perf-harness).

Out of scope: UI redesign of catalog, legacy manual publish UI.
acceptance_criteria: CI pipeline consumes benchmarking artifacts and generates a signed profile manifest with required slice metadata
New profile appears in catalog with region-normalized cost and slice tags within 24 hours of CI completion
Automated pin mapping can be evaluated by the routing layer to select the appropriate variant for a given request slice
Re-verification jobs run on schedule and create drift alerts when latency/cost regressions exceed thresholds
Runbook documented and linked; first on-call rotation can follow rollback steps and observe profile health in Console

2026-02-24 — Luca Moreno: Eng alignment meeting. Action items: (1) ENG-19101 to expose hardware metadata from benchmark jobs, (2) ENG-20345 to add signed-manifest storage in S3 and hook to registry. Luca to own integration. Agreed sample size target: min 1k samples per slice for p95 validity.

2026-02-27 — Priya Shah (SRE): Raised concern about re-verification cadence; recommended initial cadence of 7 days with anomaly window for high-usage models. Logged SRE runbook PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/128

2026-03-01 — Data Science (Marta Lo): Shared cost-normalization model and FX source. Proposed normalization to USD and cost-per-1000-tokens metric. Provided spreadsheet: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/Perf/CostModel

2026-03-03 — Luka Petrov (Security): Verified that signed-profile format meets audit requirements pending minor schema addition for key rotation. Security review flagged key-rotation automation (tied to release runtime-2.1).
notes: Trade-offs discussed: heavier sampling reduces false positives but increases chargeback costs for benchmarking; decided to tier sample sizes by model usage tier (free-tier sample smaller).
Edge-case: small-batch ultra-low-latency slices may produce noisy p95; plan to surface both p50 and p95 with sample-size confidence and require human steward sign-off for extremely low-sample slices.
Monitoring: add perf-profile.health metric and a Slack alert channel #perf-profiles-alerts. Include links to Grafana dashboards and SLO dashboards in runbook.
